## Judgment

### Expected-drift set
All four NixOS hosts (sweet16, petunia, avina, hermes) consume `core-users`,
and avina/hermes additionally carry their own per-host authorizedKeys blocks.
All four were expected to drift. The three standalone HM configs
(groot@dualie, groot@forge, groot@rk3588) touch no user SSH keys and were
expected to be static.

### Actual vs expected
Matches exactly. verify-drift.sh HEAD~1..HEAD reports DRIFT on sweet16,
petunia, avina, hermes and none on groot@dualie / groot@forge
(groot@rk3588 N/A — aarch64, not evaluated on this builder).

Recursive derivation comparison on avina: 12553 derivations by name on both
sides, with an empty name-set diff — no package added, removed, or version
-changed. Exactly five store paths differ, and they are a single clean
cascade:

  ddukes-authorized_keys.drv
  groot-authorized_keys.drv
    -> etc.drv
    -> activate.drv
    -> nixos-system-unnamed-lxc-proxmox.drv

Nothing outside the authorized_keys -> etc -> activation chain moved. This is
the minimal possible drift for an authorizedKeys edit.

Content verified by evaluation, not inference:
`nixosConfigurations.avina.config.users.users.ddukes.openssh.authorizedKeys.keys`
resolves to exactly three `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256` entries (sony, ddukes@sweet16,
ddukes@petunia). The `ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3...GQp6H` portable key is absent from
the evaluated result.

### Operational note
This removes the last non-TPM personal key fleet-wide. After deploy,
interactive ddukes@/groot@ SSH requires a TPM-sealed key from sweet16,
petunia, or sony. Root deploys are unaffected — they authenticate with
ephemeral Vault SSH certificates, not these authorized_keys entries, so a
failed personal-key assumption cannot lock the deploy path out.

Verdict: expected drift, approved for deploy.
